rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while ensuring strongly retained compounds elute. The moderate temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction.

Reduce gradient steepness while keeping the solvent window and temperature fixed to test whether the crowded central pairs separate with slope. The first run's retention window suggests this should keep the last peak near 10 minutes.

Shift the gradient start upward while keeping nearly the same slope as the fully resolved second run. This should bring the last peak below 10 minutes while largely preserving the critical pair's resolution.

Use a shallower slope to lift the remaining critical pair above R = 1.5, offsetting the added retention by raising the starting organic fraction. This targets full resolution with the last peak still below 10 minutes.
Injection 4 already reaches the maximum CRF. Raise temperature one step to seek a shorter fully resolved separation while testing the critical pair's temperature sensitivity.

Keep injection 4 as the maximum-score fallback and test a substantially faster high-temperature method. The critical pair converged at 45 C; 60 C may separate it again after an elution-order reversal, while the shorter gradient reduces analysis time.

Back off to 55 C to separate the newly crowded pair, and modestly flatten the gradient to support resolution elsewhere. This tests a faster alternative to injection 4 while retaining ample margin below 10 minutes.

Hold temperature and solvent endpoints fixed to test whether a shallower gradient resolves the remaining close pair at 55 C. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, with the other central pair monitored for possible convergence.

Slightly steepen the successful 55 C gradient by shortening it and lowering its endpoint together. Interpolation between injections 7 and 8 suggests the critical pair can remain above R = 1.5 while the last peak elutes earlier.
Shift both solvent endpoints upward by 0.05, preserving injection 9's gradient slope while seeking earlier elution. Check whether the early peaks and both close central pairs retain R ≥ 1.5.

The critical central pair worsened sharply when the starting organic fraction increased. Lower phi0 to improve that selectivity and early-peak retention, while using a steeper gradient to target a shorter fully resolved run than injection 9.

Shorten injection 11's gradient by one grid step while holding temperature and endpoints fixed. This tests whether its fully resolved separation can be accelerated further without losing either critical central pair.

Use a slope between injections 11 and 12, targeting R just above 1.5 for the limiting pair and a last peak around 7.8 minutes. The narrower solvent window should still contain every peak within the gradient.

Test a faster, steeper gradient at 60 C, where the crowded middle pair may separate after reversing elution order. Keep phi0 at 0.10 to protect early-peak retention, with injection 13 retained as the fastest fully resolved method so far.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity with a short gradient, since the higher-temperature fast methods retain a problematic middle pair. This tests a different elution-order regime while the stronger starting solvent helps offset increased retention.

Increase phi0 relative to injection 14 to shift the close middle pair farther apart after its apparent order reversal. This tests a roughly five-minute separation while checking that the following pair and early peaks remain resolved.

Lower the starting organic fraction to improve the slope-sensitive middle pair, while steepening the gradient relative to injection 13. This tests whether full resolution can be retained in a shorter run; the other central pair is the main risk.

Test intermediate low-temperature selectivity, since 25 C caused several overlaps whereas 40 C resolved well with a shallower gradient. This scouting run targets another potentially faster fully resolved regime, retaining injection 17 as the fastest maximum-score method.

Test the unexplored 50 C selectivity regime with a fast gradient and low starting organic fraction. A steeper slope may separate the temperature-sensitive central pair after its order reversal while avoiding the different overlap seen at 60 C.

Trim injection 17's unused high-organic tail while preserving its successful gradient slope. The last peak's estimated elution fraction is about 0.57, so a 0.65 endpoint should retain full resolution and the same elution time with a shorter programmed gradient.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction improves the temperature-sensitive central pair at 50 C enough for a much faster separation. Early-peak compression is the main risk; injection 20 remains a fully resolved maximum-score fallback.

Slightly steepen the fastest fully resolved gradient, from 0.075 to 0.080 organic fraction per minute. This tests the resolution boundary for a shorter maximum-score run, with injection 20 retained if the limiting pair falls below 1.5.

Refine the successful 0.10-start method with a slope between injections 12 and 13. This targets a slightly shorter separation than injection 13 while testing whether its limiting pair still reaches R = 1.5.

Test whether further steepening at 60 C opens the remaining close pair after its elution-order reversal. This is a final fast-method exploration; injection 20 already secures the maximum CRF with all peaks resolved.

Back off one endpoint step from injection 23 to restore full resolution, targeting approximately R = 1.6 for both critical pairs and a last peak near 8 minutes. This final refinement seeks more resolution margin than the fastest maximum-score method while remaining comfortably below the time-penalty threshold.
